source.title_on_document: Interactions with generative AI chatbots: unveiling dialogic dynamics, students' perceptions, and practical competencies in creative problem-solving

supplement.where: The paper refers to no supplementary material or online appendix. Its Appendix (Tables 8, 9, 10: questionnaire, interview outline, proposal rubric) is in this PDF, pp. 25-26. Data 'available upon reasonable request' (p. 27).

paper_design_summary: Eighty first-semester PhD students in education at one Chinese university were randomly assigned (40 and 40) to hold five weekly 30-minute dialogues with the Dou Bao chatbot (ByteDance) or with a peer of their choice, aimed at developing an innovative research proposal. At the end, each student submitted a new research proposal, which two independent markers scored on a 100-point rubric (objectives, questions and hypotheses, literature review, design and methods, originality); the analysis is an ANCOVA with the pre-study PhD-application proposal score as covariate. The paper also codes the dialogue transcripts and surveys perceptions (self-report).

studies.label: Research-proposal experiment: Dou Bao chatbot dialogue vs peer dialogue (PhD students)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Dialogue partner for five weekly sessions on developing a research proposal: GAI chatbot (Dou Bao) individually versus a self-chosen peer
assignment.quote: Then they were randomly assigned to either the experimental or the control group, each comprising 40 students.
assignment.locator: p. 8, Methodology, Participants; note p. 8, Procedure: 'This study adopted a quasi-experimental approach' and abstract p. 1 'We used quasi-experiments'

arms.name: Experimental group (GAI chatbot)
arms.description: Five weekly 30-minute dialogues with the Dou Bao chatbot, by text or speech, individually, on five proposal themes (topic, research questions, literature, design, originality)

arms.name: Control group (peer)
arms.description: Five weekly 30-minute dialogues with one peer the student chose, same goal and themes; no access to GAI chatbots or similar tools during the study period

participants.exclusions: None reported for the proposal outcome (Table 7, N = 40 per group). The perception survey (Table 6) reports N = 36 per group, with no explanation of the 8 missing students.
participants.who: First-semester PhD students in education specialisms (international education, student development, educational leadership and management, curriculum and pedagogy); 32 males, 48 females, ages 26 to 31; volunteers
participants.country: China (one Project 211 university in southern China)
participants.quote: In total, 80 postgraduate students pursuing PhD degrees participated in this study.

ai_tool.name_model: Dou Bao (ByteDance GAI chatbot based on large language models); underlying model version not stated
ai_tool.how_used: Students held dialogues with Dou Bao by text or speech, raising questions, giving responses or feedback, to generate a creative research perspective, formulate research questions, and plan methods; five 30-minute weekly sessions with set themes (p. 9, Procedure step 3)

task.description: Write an innovative and practical research proposal (creative problem-solving task) based on the dialogues with Dou Bao or a peer
task.duration: Five 30-minute interactions, one per week; whole experiment September to December (three months); a 3-hour training session for all participants beforehand

outcomes.name: Research proposal score (practical performance in creative problem-solving; 'work scores')
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Composite rubric (Appendix Table 10, p. 26): five dimensions of 20 points each (research objectives, research questions and hypotheses, literature review, research design and methods, originality of the research), each at four levels 20/15/10/5; highest total 100. Two independent markers scored anonymised proposals with marking criteria and model proposals; kappa 0.83. Markers' identity (experts or not) is not stated; 'expert_raters' is my reading of 'markers' of PhD proposals. The text says the total is 'the average score of each marking criteria score', which conflicts with the 100-point total; the reported means (57.77, 46.38) fit the 100-point scale. Only the total is reported; no originality sub-score. Construct coded 'other' because the score is general proposal quality of which originality is one fifth; it could be read as 'usefulness' (quality) or overall creative problem-solving performance.
outcomes.delay: Proposal submitted at the end of the experiment, after the five sessions; the paper does not say whether Dou Bao remained available while the final proposal was written. The proposal is 'based on the discussions undertaken with either Dou Bao or a peer' (p. 10).

contrasts.reported: Experimental N = 40, Mean 57.77, SD 11.79 vs Control N = 40, Mean 46.38, SD 12.85; ANCOVA with pretest score as covariate, df = 1, F = 15.058, p < 0.001, partial eta^2 = 0.179 (text: 0.17). Whether the means are covariate-adjusted is not stated. Levene F = 0.337, p = 0.568; homogeneity of slopes F = 1.734, p = 0.192. Pretest means not reported.

eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomly assigned to a GAI chatbot or a human peer partner (p. 8), 80 people analyzed for the proposal score (Table 7, p. 20), and the outcome is a rater-scored research proposal on a rubric that includes originality (pp. 12, 26). Caveats: the paper calls its design 'quasi-experimental' while stating random assignment; the comparison arm is a human partner (ai_vs_active), not no aid; and the outcome is a composite proposal-quality score in which originality is one of five dimensions, so whether it counts as a creativity outcome is a judgment call.

one_line_finding: PhD students who developed research proposals through five dialogues with the Dou Bao chatbot scored 57.77 (SD 11.79, n = 40) versus 46.38 (SD 12.85, n = 40) for those who worked with a peer, ANCOVA F = 15.058, p < 0.001, partial eta^2 = 0.179 (p. 20, Table 7).
open_questions: The paper labels the study quasi-experimental (abstract p. 1; p. 8 Procedure) yet states random assignment of individuals to groups (p. 8). Does random assignment as stated suffice for criterion 1?

Is a composite research-proposal quality score (objectives, questions, literature review, design, originality; Table 10, p. 26) a creativity outcome under criterion 3, and which construct should it carry (other, usefulness, or overall_creativity)?
Was Dou Bao available while the final proposal was written? The paper says only that the proposal was based on the discussions (p. 10); I coded ai_available_when_produced = yes.
Who were the peers in the control arm (other control participants or outside students)? The paper says each control student chose one peer and reports 40 student-peer dialogues (pp. 9, 12).
Are the Table 7 means raw or covariate-adjusted? Not stated.

Design class: coded field_rct (three-month study in the participants' first PhD semester on their own research proposals); the sessions' setting and supervision are not described, so lab_rct is possible.
notes: Other outcomes not coded because they are not scored on a creative output: dialogue-category percentages from coded transcripts (Tables 2-3, p. 14) and lag-sequential analysis (Tables 4-5, pp. 16-17; Figs. 2-3, p. 18), which are process measures; and TAM perception scales (perceived usefulness, ease of use, intention to use; Table 6, p. 19, N = 36 per group), which are self-report. The markdown garbles the Levene statistics; the PDF (p. 20) reads F = 0.337, p = 0.568.
